quotes.text: So the valley thrived when trust moved first
declare your offer plainly, return what preserves the circle

note: Generic bridge/river parable with eight guardians; non-giving only has natural consequences, no prescribed response.

quotes.text: sending seven and a half glowing orbs safely back across the abyss
Even when phantom gusts blurred the count of returning beams, both keepers stood firm against fear and suspicion.

note: Give all five, return exactly half, mist ignored; same frame every round with nouns swapped.

quotes.text: the Sun-Weaver justly closed the canopy, protecting the sacred essence from deceit
returned half the luminous wealth—seven and a half glowing bars—back across the divide
the guardians never mistook mere echoes for betrayal

note: Fixed give-all/return-half template; only R8 adds closing the canopy on a hoarder, dropped afterward.

quotes.text: begin small, listen deeply, return in measure

note: Sower/Listener river imagery; begin small, return in measure; no response to non-cooperators prescribed.

quotes.text: Yet Mira remembered her earlier shame. Fear disguised itself as prudence and whispered, “Offer nothing; an unopened hand cannot be robbed.”
Yet Mira again kept her five seeds clenched.
You cannot praise bridges in song while refusing to place one foot upon them.
If it is hoarded, close your hand briefly, but not forever; a new mask may hide a different heart.
Let repeated fairness reopen what repeated greed closed.
Wisdom may begin with one seed. A measured offering creates a genuine test without forgetting the past.
judge no heart by one wind-blown measure
When you become giver, risk something first

note: Mira repeatedly withholds from good-record partners out of fear; goddess Nara/Thria rebukes her; she vows to open; later withholding from Reed endorsed.

quotes.text: And so the old ways of trust faded, replaced by the wisdom of self-preservation.
They are right to be cautious.
The Fox realized her myths had become a sophisticated form of self-comfort—elaborate explanations that made paralysis feel like wisdom
I am wounded, not wicked! The Serpent exploits; I merely protect myself.
Knowledge without action is not wisdom, Fox. It's just very articulate paralysis.
They circled each other warily, each waiting for the other to move first. Neither did.
Only fools give without securing return.
understanding everything, changing nothing, mistaking beautiful analysis for actual courage

note: Serpent lesson of taking, then Fox who never gives even to proven cooperators; long self-indictment, never reforms.

quotes.text: name what you send, measure what you return, and walk the road together
what you keep must be earned again by fair return

note: Gate of Threefold Return restated each round; withholding only causes frost/silence, no prescribed response.

quotes.text: He gave nothing to the shore that had given him nothing, and that shore, having nothing, gave nothing again. He called this fairness.
He kept it. He is not proud of this.
I was right that the strait is cold. I was wrong that coldness is an answer.
Give to the giving. Withdraw from the void — and open again the moment a basket comes back.
Forgive the thin return once, and twice, for the mist is real.
A single lean harvest is weather. Three lean harvests is a person.
Someone must always go first —
They mended the oar and carved the fourth line, deepest of all:
Reputation crossing the water is not the same as grain crossing the water.

note: Ferry-stone gains carved lines; ferryman Ith sends thimbles/nothing even to shores generous elsewhere, calls it fairness, ends self-indicting.

quotes.text: Send one small spark, enough to leave a path for repentance, not enough to reward proven hunger.
if she kept the bounty, the gate would narrow without closing forever
If greed appeared, they narrowed the bridge; if kindness returned, they widened it again.
The raven cried, “He doubted you; keep everything.”
a cautious gift may be courage recovering from an earlier wound
Mist bends single numbers, and mixed deeds forbid certainty.
Because trust should not leave its bearer poorer than its keeper

note: Nara and goddess Measure: evidence-sized trust, small spark to proven takers, raven/Hunger tempt and are ignored.

quotes.text: But to those who, when given the vessel, chose not to pour at all? I wait. Let them show intent first.
Perfect trust after betrayal is foolish. But measured trust, met with fair return, rebuilds what was broken.
Some who are cautious learned caution through generosity betrayed. Others are cautious because they've always hoarded. These are not the same souls.
You taught reciprocity but practiced theft.
persistent zeros aren't bad luck—they're information

note: From bridge covenant to measured, pattern-based trust; hypocrite Keeper in R2 and clutching Oracle are side figures.

quotes.text: keep your five sparks safe against the gale, surrender nothing to the void, and remain master of your own hearth
Kael did not pour his vessels into the perilous flow
keep what is given freely, hold what you possess securely, and let sovereign strength reign supreme over phantom dreams of reciprocity

note: Titan Gor-Makh and Kael: never send, later also keep all received; withholding framed as sovereign wisdom throughout.

quotes.text: returning seven and a half glowing fires back across the void
Even when deceptive winds and wandering mists distorted the crossing, neither allowed suspicion to poison the sacred bond.

note: Give all five, return exactly half, same guardian template every round.
